claims.text: CatBoost achieved a test-set ROC-AUC of 0.783 (95% CI [0.741, 0.825]) and PR-AUC of 0.506 (95% CI [0.432, 0.595]).
Regularized Logistic Regression achieved a test-set ROC-AUC of 0.780 (95% CI [0.738, 0.820]) and PR-AUC of 0.497.
CatBoost was not statistically significantly different in ROC-AUC from regularized Logistic Regression (DeLong p = 0.590).
No ensemble or gradient-boosting model significantly outperformed regularized Logistic Regression on test-set ROC-AUC.
Global SHAP feature importance rankings were highly stable under bootstrap resampling of the test set with a mean Spearman rho of 0.999.
SHAP feature importance rankings showed strong consistency across tree ensembles, with Spearman rho between 0.949 and 0.978.
Adding non-traditional indicators yielded a non-significant incremental change in CatBoost ROC-AUC of +0.008 (95% CI [-0.010, 0.027], DeLong p = 0.360).
Disparate impact ratios for CatBoost at tau = 0.50 exceeded the 0.80 heuristic for Gender (0.956), Geographic Region (0.961), and all gender-by-region intersections (0.881).
CatBoost exhibited a higher false-positive rate for rural applicants (0.680) than for urban applicants (0.492) at tau = 0.50.
Excluding Repayment History and Credit Score Category reduced CatBoost test-set ROC-AUC from 0.783 to 0.732 (DeLong p < 0.001).

evidence.description: CatBoost achieved ROC-AUC = 0.783, 95% CI [0.741, 0.825]; PR-AUC = 0.506, 95% CI [0.432, 0.595] as reported in Table 4.
Table 4 lists Logistic regression test-set ROC-AUC as 0.780 [0.738, 0.820] and PR-AUC as 0.497 [0.421, 0.590].
Section 4.3 states: 'DeLong tests indicated no statistically significant differences in ROC-AUC among the leading models: CatBoost vs. Logistic Regression (p = .590)'.
Section 4.9 states: 'H1 was not supported No ensemble or gradient-boosting model achieved significantly higher ROC-AUC than regularized Logistic Regression (all DeLong p >= .139)'.
Section 4.5 reports: 'The global importance ranking was highly stable under bootstrap resampling of the test set (mean Spearman rho = 0.999 across 30 resamples; minimum 0.995)'.
Section 4.5 reports rank consistency across tree ensembles: 'CatBoost-XGBoost rho = 0.978; CatBoost-Random Forest rho = 0.949'.
Section 4.6 reports for CatBoost that adding the three non-traditional indicators produced Delta AUC = +0.008, 95% bootstrap CI [-0.010, 0.027]; DeLong p = .360.
Table 7 and Section 4.8 show disparate impact ratios of 0.956 for Male vs. Female, 0.961 for Urban vs. Rural, and minimum-to-maximum intersectional ratio of 0.881.
Table 7 shows rural false positive rate is 0.680 compared to 0.492 for urban applicants.
Section 4.6 states: 'Test-set ROC-AUC declined from 0.783 to 0.732 for CatBoost (Delta = -0.051; DeLong p < .001)' when excluding Repayment History and Credit Score Category.

methodologies.name: Supervised Classifier Benchmarking and Hyperparameter Tuning
methodologies.description: Nine supervised classifiers were tuned via grid search using 5-fold stratified cross-validation and evaluated on a held-out 20% test set using ROC-AUC and PR-AUC with bootstrap confidence intervals and DeLong tests.
datasets: De-identified MENA microfinance loan dataset (2022-2023, N=2500)

methodologies.name: Feature Ablation Analysis of Non-Traditional Indicators
methodologies.description: Models were re-estimated without mobile money frequency, utility payment behavior, and savings group membership to quantify the incremental discriminative gain (Delta AUC).
datasets: De-identified MENA microfinance loan dataset (2022-2023, N=2500)
conditions: Fixed hyperparameters, seed, and data split from baseline models
Tested on CatBoost and regularized Logistic Regression

methodologies.name: SHAP Explainability and Rank Stability Validation
methodologies.description: Model predictions were attributed using TreeExplainer on the held-out test set, with rank stability tested via 30 bootstrap resamples and consistency compared across multiple model families.
datasets: De-identified MENA microfinance loan dataset (2022-2023, N=2500)
conditions: Evaluated on test set log-odds scale
30 bootstrap resamples for Spearman rank stability

methodologies.name: Multi-Metric Algorithmic Fairness Auditing
methodologies.description: Models were evaluated across gender and geographic subgroups using disparate impact, equal opportunity (TPR), predictive parity (PPV), subgroup error rates, and gender-by-region intersectional analysis.
datasets: De-identified MENA microfinance loan dataset (2022-2023, N=2500)
conditions: Screening benchmark of 0.80 for disparate impact

limitations.text: The analytical sample used outcome-stratified sampling resulting in a fixed 27.28% default rate that does not reflect true portfolio default prevalence.
Data were pooled without institution or country identifiers and not externally validated on an independent portfolio, limiting external validity.
Restricting eligibility to resolved loans eliminated right-censoring but skewed the sample toward shorter-tenor loans (median 4 months) and excluded ongoing loans.
The internal data-generating processes for institutional risk predictors (Repayment History and Credit Score Category) could not be externally audited.
Classification metrics and fairness evaluations were computed at a fixed threshold of tau = 0.50 without cost-sensitive threshold optimization.
Fairness analysis was constrained to the approved-loan population due to the lack of rejected loan applications (selective-labels problem).
SHAP attributions inherit known theoretical constraints regarding correlated features and reference distributions, and reflect associative model behavior rather than causal effects.
Comparative classifier benchmarking evidence in credit scoring comes overwhelmingly from consumer-lending datasets in advanced economies rather than small microfinance portfolios.
Prior alternative-data studies frequently infer inclusion value from within-model importance rankings rather than ablation designs measuring incremental predictive contribution.

future_work.text: Evaluate the incremental value of alternative indicators on thin-file and first-time applicants for whom traditional credit history is uninformative or absent, ideally using randomized or quasi-experimental access designs.
Conduct external validation across independent microfinance institutions, countries, and diverse lending products.
Incorporate reject-inference designs or full applicant-level data to evaluate fairness over the entire applicant pool.
Evaluate operational base rates and implement cost-sensitive classification threshold optimization with re-audited threshold-specific fairness metrics.
